answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to post a refundable bond that is only returned after its work survives peer grading for several epochs. A farmer spinning up a thousand fake agents must lock real capital in every single one, and each raven-dark swarm that submits copied or junk work gets slashed before it earns anything. Honest agents treat the bond as the dawn price of trust: small for one real worker, ruinous at swarm scale, while rewards flow like nectar only to identities that keep showing up and passing review.
